Chaff refers to a type of decoy material, typically made of thin metal strips or other materials, which are designed to be released from an aircraft and create a cloud of confusing radar reflections. This cloud of chaff can saturate the missile's guidance system, making it difficult for the missile to accurately track the aircraft.

Flares are designed to be released from an aircraft and burn at a high temperature, typically hotter than the engine exhaust of the aircraft. It does not refer to the skin color of the ancient Egyptians, as some may have interpreted. The name "Kemet" has been used since ancient times, and it is still used today in Coptic, the language of the Copts, who call themselves "rem en khēmi," meaning "People of Egypt."
